title.en: Transpiration and the opening and closing of stomata

hook.en: A large tree can lose a few hundred litres of water a day through tiny pores in its leaves. It seems wasteful, yet the same pores let in the carbon dioxide the plant must have.

objectives.en: Explain how stomata open and close
List factors affecting transpiration and its significance

narration.en: A large tree can lose a few hundred litres of water a day through tiny pores in its leaves. It seems wasteful, yet the same pores let in the carbon dioxide the plant must have.

body.en: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant, mostly through stomata (also some through the cuticle and lenticels). Each stoma has two guard cells. When K⁺ ions move in, water follows by osmosis, the guard cells become turgid and, because their inner walls are thick and the cellulose microfibrils run radially, they bow outward and open the pore. When they lose K⁺ and water, the pore closes. Stomata usually open by day and close at night; ABA closes them in water stress.

points.en: Thick inner walls and radial microfibrils make them bow

narration.en: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from the aerial parts of a plant, mostly through stomata (also some through the cuticle and lenticels). Each stoma has two guard cells. When K⁺ ions move in, water follows by osmosis, the guard cells become turgid and, because their inner walls are thick and the cellulose microfibrils run radially, they bow outward and open the pore. When they lose K⁺ and water, the pore closes. Stomata usually open by day and close at night; ABA closes them in water stress.
More light opens the pore; water stress and ABA close it. A wide pore lets CO₂ in but also lets water out: the plant must balance the two.

caption.en: Set the light and the water supply. The guard cells take up K⁺ and water in light, and lose them when water is short. The pore width sets the rate of transpiration and of CO₂ uptake.

tryThis.en: Turn the light to zero. What happens to the pore?
Bright light but very dry soil: does the stoma open?
Raise the humidity. Why does transpiration fall even with an open pore?

say.en: A guard cell's inner wall, beside the pore, is thick and stiff; the outer wall is thin.
Water enters; the thin outer wall stretches more, so each cell bends outward and the pore widens.
Radial cellulose microfibrils also help: they let the cell lengthen and pull the inner wall outward.

text.en: K⁺ in → water in → turgid → open

body.en: External factors: light (opens stomata), temperature (faster evaporation), humidity (slows it), wind (removes the humid layer and speeds it). Internal factors: number and distribution of stomata, the proportion open, water status, canopy and leaf structure. Transpiration creates the pull for water and mineral uptake, cools leaves by evaporation, and keeps cells turgid. It is the price of photosynthesis: stomata open for CO₂ and lose water. C₄ plants fix CO₂ more efficiently and lose about half as much water per unit of CO₂ fixed.

points.en: Transpiration is water loss as vapour, mostly through stomata.
K⁺ uptake makes guard cells turgid; their thick inner walls make them bow apart and open the pore; ABA closes it.
Light, heat and wind speed transpiration; humidity slows it; it drives the transpiration pull and cools the leaf.
